title: In Loud, Exalted Strains
description: In Loud, Exalted Strains in Tonic Solfa to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Benjamin Francis wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 457.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR); any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: In loud, ex-alt-ed strains, The King of Glo-ry praise; O’er heav’n and earth He reigns Through ev-er-last-ing days; But Zi-on, with His pre-sence blest, Is His de-light, His cho-sen rest.

lines: O’er heav’n and earth He reigns
But Zion, with His presence blest,
Is His delight, His chosen rest.
Beneath this roof vouchsafe to show
How God can dwell with men below.
Now let Thy Gospel’s joyful sound
Till all who humbly seek Thy face

licence: Public domain: Benjamin Francis died in 1799.
credits: Words by Benjamin Francis (1734–1799), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
